title: Unleashing the Power of T1-cells in SFQ Arithmetic Circuits
problem: Gate-level pipelining in SFQ systems incurs significant area overhead due to path balancing requirements, and this overhead is particularly detrimental given the limited layout density inherent to RSFQ technology.
motivation: RSFQ technology offers orders of magnitude smaller power dissipation than conventional electronics, making it attractive for cloud computing, aerospace electronics, and quantum computing interfaces.
method: The paper proposes T1-cells as specialized circuit primitives for SFQ arithmetic circuits to address path balancing and area overhead. T1-cells are designed to reduce the area penalty of pipelining in SFQ systems by optimizing the gate-level implementation and layout density.
key_novelty: Introduction of T1-cells as a circuit primitive to mitigate pipelining area overhead and improve layout efficiency in SFQ arithmetic operations.
contributions: T1-cell design for SFQ arithmetic circuits
Reduced area overhead in pipelined SFQ systems
Improved physical layout density for RSFQ implementations
